                                      RELATED CASE ORDER




       A Motion for Administrative Relief to Consider Whether Cases Should be Related or a Sua
Sponte Judicial Referral for Purpose of Determining Relationship (Civil L.R. 3-12) has been filed.
The time for filing an opposition or statement of support has passed. As the judge assigned to
case



        25-cv-02095-JST

        I find that the more recently filed case(s) that I have initialed below are related to the
case assigned to me, and such case(s) shall be reassigned to me. Any cases listed below that are
not related to the case assigned to me are referred to the judge assigned to the next-earliest
filed case for a related case determination.




Case                 Title                    Related Not Related

25-cv-02197-HSG A.M. v. ProctorU, Inc.          JST

         The parties are instructed that all future filings in any reassigned case are to bear the
initials of the newly assigned judge immediately after the case number. Any case management
conference in any reassigned case will be rescheduled by the Court. The parties shall adjust the
dates for the conference, disclosures and report required by FRCivP 16 and 26 accordingly.

noticed by the moving party before the newly assigned judge; any deadlines set by the ADR Local
Rules remain in effect; and any deadlines established in a case management order continue to
govern, except dates for appearance in court, which will be rescheduled by the newly assigned
judge.

                                                                   23                 Plaintiff Trisha A.M. (“Plaintiff”), individually and on behalf of all others
                                                                   24   similarly situated, brings this Complaint against Defendant ProctorU, Inc. d/b/a Meazure
                                                                   25   Learning (“Defendant”). Plaintiff alleges the following based on (a) personal knowledge, (b)
                                                                   26   the investigation of counsel, and (c) information and belief.
                                                                   27   ///
                                                                   28   ///

                                                                                                               1
                                                                                                    CLASS ACTION COMPLAINT
                                                                               Case 4:25-cv-02197         Document 1    Filed 03/03/25    Page 2 of 16



                                                                    1                                         INTRODUCTION
                                                                    2          1.     Plaintiff, individually and on behalf of all others similarly situated, brings this
                                                                    3   action against Defendant for its failure to properly administer the February 2025 California
                                                                    4   Bar Examination (“Bar Exam”), resulting in severe technical failures that deprived test-takers
                                                                    5   of a fair examination process.
                                                                    6          2.     As the Court is undoubtedly aware, the bar exam is a time of extreme stress, and
                                                                    7   success or failure often has a direct impact on test-takers’ future employment opportunities.
                                                                    8   Moreover, students study for months, and spend substantial amounts of money with various
                                                                    9   bar prep test companies, in order to maximize their chances of passing the bar exam and finally
                                                                   10   becoming a licensed attorney.
                                                                   11          3.     Defendant contracted with the State Bar of California to provide remote
NYE, STIRLING, HALE, MILLER & SWEET




                                                                   12   proctoring software that all individuals that used a computer were required to download,
                               SANTA BARBARA, CALIFORNIA 93101
                               33 WEST MISSION STREET, SUITE 201




                                                                   13   install, and run during the bar exam, which it refers to as the “Meazure Learning platform”
                                                                   14   (hereafter, the “software”). For the privilege of using Defendant’s software, Plaintiff and the
                                                                   15   putative class were required to pay a fee to Defendant.
                                                                   16          4.     The February 2025 bar exam, however, was a complete disaster, and Plaintiff
                                                                   17   and the Class experienced a slew of issues with Defendant’s software that negatively impacted
                                                                   18   their ability to complete the bar exam, including: software crashes that took minutes or hours
                                                                   19   to resolve, server crashes, the inability to copy/paste material, typos within the bar exam
                                                                   20   questions caused by software glitches, software freezes, large queues that prevented the ability
                                                                   21   to get back into the software, software glitches with the identity verification and security
                                                                   22   checks, disconnections from the software with the inability to reconnect, and other serious
                                                                   23   software issues.
                                                                   24          5.     Defendant’s failure to ensure the proper exam administration has caused
                                                                   25   substantial harm to Plaintiff and class members, including financial loss, emotional distress,
                                                                   26   and professional setbacks.
                                                                   27          6.     Plaintiff seeks damages, declaratory relief, and an injunction requiring
                                                                   28   Defendant to take corrective measures to prevent similar failures in future examinations.

                                                                                                                2
                                                                                                     CLASS ACTION COMPLAINT
                                                                               Case 4:25-cv-02197        Document 1      Filed 03/03/25     Page 3 of 16



                                                                    1                                   JURISDICTION AND VENUE
                                                                    2          7.      This Court has subject matter jurisdiction over the claims asserted herein
                                                                    3   pursuant to the Class Action Fairness Act, 28 U.S.C. §1332(d)(2), because Plaintiff and some
                                                                    4   of the members of the proposed classes are citizens of a State different from that of the
                                                                    5   Defendant and, upon the original filing of this Complaint, members of the putative class
                                                                    6   resided in states around the country; there are more than 100 putative class members; and the
                                                                    7   amount in controversy exceeds $5 million, exclusive of interest and costs.
                                                                    8          8.      The Court also has personal jurisdiction over the parties because Defendant
                                                                    9   conducts a major part of its national operations, advertising, and sales through continuous
                                                                   10   business activity in this District.
                                                                   11          9.      Venue is further appropriate pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §1391 because Defendant
NYE, STIRLING, HALE, MILLER & SWEET




                                                                   12   conducts business in this District, because it has specifically marketed, advertised, and
                               SANTA BARBARA, CALIFORNIA 93101
                               33 WEST MISSION STREET, SUITE 201




                                                                   13   contracted extensively in California. Venue is also proper in this Court because a substantial
                                                                   14   part of the events and actions giving rise to the harm suffered by Plaintiff and members of the
                                                                   15   proposed Class occurred in this District.
                                                                   16                                               PARTIES
                                                                   17          Plaintiff
                                                                   18          10.     Plaintiff Trisha A.M. is a resident of California who sat for the February 2025
                                                                   19   California Bar Exam.
                                                                   20          11.     Plaintiff faced significant technical and logistical difficulties throughout the
                                                                   21   exam process due to the defective software platform provided by Defendant, which
                                                                   22   substantially impaired her ability to complete the exam.
                                                                   23          12.     Prior to the exam, Plaintiff experienced technical difficulties in the registration
                                                                   24   process. The software platform failed to display any available testing locations within 50 miles
                                                                   25   of her residence, requiring her to travel 1.5 to 2 hours each way to the South San Francisco
                                                                   26   Convention Center to take the test. When Plaintiff attempted to resolve this issue, she was
                                                                   27   subjected to a cycle of misdirection between Defendant and the California Bar. Defendant’s
                                                                   28   customer support repeatedly instructed Plaintiff to contact the California Bar for assistance,

                                                                                                                 3
                                                                                                      CLASS ACTION COMPLAINT
                                                                               Case 4:25-cv-02197         Document 1      Filed 03/03/25     Page 4 of 16



                                                                    1   while the California Bar referred her back to Defendant, where the California Bar finally
                                                                    2   advised her to input a mock zip code to be able to sign up for the exam, because Defendant
                                                                    3   was unable to offer another solution.
                                                                    4          13.      On the day of the exam, Plaintiff encountered multiple software malfunctions
                                                                    5   that severely disrupted her ability to complete the test under fair and reasonable conditions.
                                                                    6   For example, the copy/paste function was inoperable, significantly delaying Plaintiff’s ability
                                                                    7   to efficiently transfer and edit text within her responses. Defendant had prior knowledge of
                                                                    8   this defect, as the same issue was reported during the January 2025 mock exam, and Defendant
                                                                    9   assured test-takers that the problem would be resolved before the actual exam date. Despite
                                                                   10   these assurances, the issue remained unresolved.
                                                                   11          14.      Plaintiff also experienced login issues and software lag, causing significant
NYE, STIRLING, HALE, MILLER & SWEET




                                                                   12   delays and interruptions during the exam.
                               SANTA BARBARA, CALIFORNIA 93101
                               33 WEST MISSION STREET, SUITE 201




                                                                   13          15.      The layout of the software was defective, requiring Plaintiff to scroll up to read
                                                                   14   the question and then scroll back down to type her response, imposing an unnecessary burden
                                                                   15   on test-takers and further slowing down the completion of the bar exam. For example, the
                                                                   16   performance test prompt opened in a separate window, which forced the Plaintiff to memorize
                                                                   17   the content of the prompt due to only being able to view one window at a time.
                                                                   18          16.      As a result of these defects, Plaintiff was forced to spend additional time
                                                                   19   navigating software malfunctions rather than focusing on answering exam questions, putting
                                                                   20   her at a significant disadvantage compared to test-takers who did not experience these issues.
                                                                   21          17.      Plaintiff’s exam was not rescheduled to accommodate these issues. Instead, the
                                                                   22   California Bar stated it would conduct a “statistical analysis” to determine how the software
                                                                   23   failures impacted scores. As of the filing of this Complaint, the California Bar has not indicated
                                                                   24   whether there will be a delay in score releases, leaving Plaintiff in a state of uncertainty.
                                                                   25          18.      Plaintiff does not have a job lined up and must now wait until May for her results.
                                                                   26   If she does not pass due to Defendant’s software failures, she will be required to retake the
                                                                   27   exam in July.
                                                                   28   ///

                                                                                                                 4
                                                                                                      CLASS ACTION COMPLAINT
                                                                               Case 4:25-cv-02197        Document 1      Filed 03/03/25    Page 5 of 16



                                                                    1             19.   Plaintiff will incur additional out-of-pocket expenses, including but not limited
                                                                    2   to hotel accommodations, travel expenses, and the cost of study materials in preparation for a
                                                                    3   retake.
                                                                    4             20.   Prior to the February exam, the California Bar preemptively offered all test-
                                                                    5   takers a waiver to retake the exam in July at no cost, signaling prior knowledge that technical
                                                                    6   failures were expected to impact test performance. Individuals reportedly withdrew from the
                                                                    7   February exam and registered for the July exam instead to avoid potential software
                                                                    8   malfunctions. However, Plaintiff did not have the same opportunity, as she only became fully
                                                                    9   aware of the software defects during the exam itself.
                                                                   10             21.   Defendant’s failure to provide a functional and reliable exam platform caused
                                                                   11   Plaintiff to suffer significant harm, including stress, financial burden, and an unfair
NYE, STIRLING, HALE, MILLER & SWEET




                                                                   12   disadvantage in a high-stakes licensing exam.
